summary: Bonner County crow's nest in a tree, dated to about 1937 on Quartz Mountain; the tree has fallen, but a standing trunk and boot pegs remain.

facts.design: 60-foot crow's nest built in a tree
facts.status_note: The crows-nest tree has fallen, year unknown; a standing trunk and a fallen trunk remain (Idaho Fire Lookouts).

access.note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists it as drive-up; firelookout.com places it in the Kaniksu National Forest; no closure or permit is described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Listed as drive-up by Idaho Fire Lookouts; the post gives no route details.

events.note: 60-foot crow's nest; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1937, Rex's page gives c.1937

evidence.supports: 60-foot crow's nest dated 1937; still there in the 1980s; labelled abandoned
the crows-nest tree has fallen; year unknown
evidence.quote: The crows-nest tree has fallen down, we arent sure what year that happened.

evidence.supports: standing and fallen trunks both still full of boot pegs
evidence.quote: the trunk that is standing, as well as the fallen trunk are both still full of boot pegs

evidence.supports: older bottles hidden in the brush below the site
evidence.quote: We found some older bottles hidden in the brush below the area.

evidence.supports: c.1937 date for the 60-foot crow's nest

corrections.why: Idaho Fire Lookouts says the crows-nest tree has fallen while the trunk that is standing remains; gone overstates the description.

notes_for_editor: Read firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts (2022 post), Rex's page and the firelookout.org Idaho list (row: Quartz Mountain, Bonner, 48.32181 -116.94819, Crowsnest Abandoned; brief coordinates match it). The 1937 date is on all three pages. The 1980s note and the Kaniksu attribution come from firelookout.com only. Abandonment date is not given by any source, so no abandoned event is recorded. Access public is inferred from the drive-up label and national forest land, not stated outright. No staffing data in any source, so none recorded. Rex's page cites Kresek; that book was not read.
